title: Swedish Historical Calendar
intro: The Swedish historical calendar models the country's exceptional transition from Julian to Gregorian dates, rather than inventing a perpetual Swedish calendar.

steps.heading: 1700: Sweden begins a gradual change
steps.text: The Julian leap day was omitted in 1700 as the first step in a planned gradual transition, making Swedish dates one day ahead of Julian dates.

steps.heading: 1712: the extra day
steps.text: Sweden abandoned the plan and restored Julian reckoning by adding an extra day in February 1712.

steps.heading: 1753: a sudden Gregorian change
steps.text: The final Gregorian switch omitted eleven local numbered dates in February 1753.

example: The local sequence 29 February 1712, 30 February 1712, 1 March 1712 is valid. Wednesday 17 February 1753 was followed by Thursday 1 March; local dates 18–28 February do not exist that year.
history: European countries adopted Gregorian labels at different times. Sweden's attempted gradual change and reversal produced a unique civil-date sequence.
model: The provider uses Julian labels before the 1700 exception, the adjusted Swedish chronology until the 1712 restoration, ordinary Julian labels until the 1753 switch and Gregorian labels thereafter.
limits: Historical date labels must be compared by their underlying day coordinate. Neighbouring countries may have labelled the same day differently.
